title: A Live Plotter: The Data Rate Is Not the Frame Rate

questions.question: A widget calls update() every time a sample arrives, from a sensor at one kilohertz. What happens?
options: The event loop spends its time preparing pictures nobody sees, and the application stops responding
The chart updates a thousand times a second and looks smooth
Qt ignores the extra calls entirely, so nothing happens
The chart falls behind the data
questions.explanation: A screen shows about sixty frames a second. Nine hundred and forty of those pictures are made and thrown away, while the click that just arrived waits.

questions.question: What should addSample do instead?
options: Record the sample and mark the picture out of date, and nothing else
Call repaint() so the drawing is not deferred
Call update() only every tenth sample
Draw directly into an image buffer
questions.explanation: Something running at the frame rate then asks for the repaint. Every tenth sample is still the data rate setting the pace, just a slower version of the same mistake.

questions.question: Why does refresh return early when nothing changed?
options: A frame timer fires whether or not data arrived, and repainting regardless burns a core redrawing an identical picture
Qt refuses repeated update calls
It avoids a flicker
It is only needed while debugging
questions.explanation: The stale flag is what turns the timer from a schedule into a permission. Leaving it out is the second version of the same mistake.

questions.question: What is the difference between update() and repaint()?
options: update asks the event loop to paint when it next can and merges requests, repaint paints immediately and merges nothing
update is for widgets and repaint is for windows
repaint is the modern spelling of update
update redraws only the changed region
questions.explanation: repaint is the right call in approximately no situation that arises in normal code, and it turns this problem from bad to unrecoverable.

questions.question: This widget has a signal and lesson 00-08's window did not. What does that change?
options: Q_OBJECT is load bearing here: without it the signal has no definition and the build fails at the link
The widget now needs an event loop
The widget can no longer be rendered offscreen
Nothing, Q_OBJECT is always required
questions.explanation: Removing the macro from the 00-08 window changed nothing observable, which is why that lesson does not claim it as a trap and this one does.

questions.question: How much of lesson 10-02's arithmetic had to change for the widget?
options: None of it, which is the reason the arithmetic and the surface were separated in the first place
The axis rules, since pixels differ from characters
The rolling window, since a widget cannot erase from a vector
The flip, which is inverted in a window
questions.explanation: That is what leaves this lesson free to be about the one thing that is genuinely new, which is how often to draw.
